**Job ID** REQ20182677 **Category** Support Services

  

In order for your application to be considered, please attach a cover letter and CV to your employment application.

  
  

The Center for Economic and Social Research (CESR) is seeking a **Public Communications Coordinator** to join its team. As part of our growing communications team, this position will work alongside another Communications Coordinator to support the team’s expanding communications and outreach efforts. The **Public Communications Coordinator** will work with a multidisciplinary team to develop and disseminate resources that promote and enable longitudinal and cross-country analyses on aging, health, and retirement, including contextualizing and communicating newly available resources and data on exposures over the lifespan that increase dementia and other disease risk. This position requires a curious communicator who can learn, distill, and disseminate complex, technical information to a wide variety of audiences.

  
  

This is a grant funded, one year fixed term position with a hybrid work arrangement.

**Job responsibilities include:**

* Developing and maintaining communications materials
  + Drafting website content and announcements (e.g., newsletters, blogs)
  + Evaluating existing resources and editing content as necessary
  + Reviewing and copy-editing research products (e.g., journal articles, policy briefs, op-eds)
  + Maintaining and growing social media presence (e.g., X, LinkedIn; developing short-form videos or posts)
  + Creating conference and event materials (e.g., brochures/flyers, exhibit posters)
* Distilling complex, technical research topics into clear, concise, and effective content to share with a variety of audiences, both technical and non-technical
* Coordinating with stakeholders to ensure timely completion and distribution of communications materials
* Reviewing and revising project resources and other written materials to ensure quality, readability, and consistency
* Experience or interest in developing a communications strategy to publicize the research project and grow its audience; this may include pitching investigators and other subject matter experts for news articles, media appearances, and op-eds
  

  

**Qualifications:**

Ability to quickly grasp complex technical concepts, make them easily understandable through varied mediums, incorporate feedback, and iteratively refine content.

  
  

Ability to collaborate effectively with numerous project stakeholders (e.g., investigators, administrative staff, university officials) at the university and with collaborators at other research institutions. Strong editing skills, ranging from developmental editing to copyediting. Graphic design experience is a plus but not required.

  
  

Minimum education: Bachelor’s Degree

  
  

Minimum Experience: 2+ years (3+ years preferred). Background in communications, public relations, marketing, or a related field is required. A background or experience working in academia or with clients in public health, economics, or policy is not required, but is preferred.

  
  

**Work Arrangement:**

Hybrid (3 days per week) on the University Park Campus in Los Angeles, CA.

**Compensation**

The hourly rate range for this position is $31.97 - $35.35. When extending an offer of employment, the University of Southern California considers factors such as (but not limited to) the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, federal, state and local laws, contractual stipulations, grant funding, as well as external market and organizational considerations.

We are hiring Sales Development Representatives to build the pipeline behind HeyGen's next phase of growth. This is a full-funnel prospecting role with a heavy emphasis on outbound. You will research target accounts, run creative outbound campaigns, work product-led signals, qualify interest, and book first meetings for our Account Executives. **Build pipeline from scratch** - You will run high-volume, high-quality outbound into target accounts. You should be excited by the idea of starting conversations that would not have happened without you.

**Mine product-led signals** - You will work with self-serve users, product usage data, sign-ups, and inbound interest to find the teams already getting value from HeyGen who are ready for a bigger conversation.

**Qualify with discipline** - You will run first conversations that uncover real pain, identify who owns the budget, and understand timing, so every meeting you book is one an Account Executive wants to take.

**Sell the outcome, not just the meeting** - You will help prospects see how HeyGen can reduce video production costs, speed up content creation, improve localization, personalize customer communication, and unlock new video workflows, so they show up to the first call already curious.

**Move fast and test** - You will try new messaging, channels, personas, and sequences, measure what works, and share it with the team. Most experiments fail; the ones that work become the playbook.

**Partner with Account Executives** - You will align with AEs on target accounts, share what you are hearing in the market, and hand off the context they need to run a strong first meeting.

**Maintain strong pipeline discipline** - You will keep CRM data clean, log activity accurately, and understand the difference between a real opportunity and a polite maybe.

* A high-agency, builder mindset. You do not wait for perfect playbooks. You test, learn, and iterate.

If "figure it out and build it from scratch" makes you lean in rather than flinch, keep reading.  
  
This is a true outside sales role. You'll be in the field at least four days a week — walking into law firms, meeting paralegals and attorneys face-to-face, working bar association events, and becoming the most familiar name in your territory for deposition services.  
  
This isn't an email job. It's not a Zoom job. You win by showing up — consistently, professionally, and with something useful to say every time. You'll also need range: the ability to build rapport in the reception area and get your foot in the door with a paralegal, and the sophistication to sit across from a managing partner and hold your own on price, value, and strategy. This is a premium-priced product in a market full of commodity providers — so you have to be able to sell the difference, not just the service. If you love the rhythm of door-to-door selling, can navigate a downtown legal corridor, and have the discipline to run a territory like your own small business, you'll thrive here. There is no ceiling on your earnings

### **What You'll Do**

* Build the playbook. As the first rep in your territory, you'll test what works, document it, and help shape the model Filevine scales from. Your wins and your lessons both matter.
* Own a defined geographic territory and build a daily route plan that maximizes face-to-face time with litigation attorneys, paralegals, legal assistants, and firm administrators.

Logistics Coordinator II
========================

**Location:** Onsite – Pleasanton, California  
**Reporting to:** Logistics Manager

Our mission is to help organizations thrive in a rapidly evolving technology landscape through strategic insight, cutting-edge solutions, and a security-first mindset. We provide end-to-end services spanning cloud consulting, AI infrastructure, and enterprise security, enabling secure, scalable, and future-ready transformation.  
  
As trusted advisors, we align IT investments with business outcomes that drive performance and growth, starting with deep strategic engagement and delivering tailored solutions built for long-term impact.  
  
Our approach is innovation-led and rooted in cybersecurity, with a focus on leveraging the right technologies to solve real-world challenges. We invest in our people and foster a culture of growth, inclusion, and purpose because we believe empowered teams build transformative technology.  
  
**Overview**  
The Logistics Coordinator II is responsible for supporting warehouse operations, shipping and receiving, RMA parts handling and vendor returns, asset and inventory management, and day-to-day facilities coordination. This role serves as a key operational resource for inventory tracking, equipment receiving and outbound shipments, vendor and ticket coordination, and warehouse organization. The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, hands-on, and comfortable working in fast-paced operational and warehouse environments while supporting both internal teams and customer-related initiatives.

Key Responsibilities
--------------------

**Warehouse & Facilities Operations**

* Maintain warehouse organization including shelving, inventory placement, labeling, and cleanliness.
* Coordinate and support office and warehouse operational needs.
* Ensure warehouse areas remain clean, safe, and operationally efficient.
* Organize and maintain inventory storage areas for internal equipment and customer consignments.
* Support facilities coordination tasks as assigned.

**Shipping & Logistics**

* Coordinate shipping and receiving activities for internal and customer equipment.
* Palletize equipment for outbound shipments and deployment preparation.
* Perform FedEx drop-offs and support smaller shipment logistics.
* Validate incoming shipping orders and ensure order accuracy.
* Receive, organize, and shelve shipments after consignments are created by the sales team.
* Track shipment status and coordinate with internal stakeholders to ensure timely processing.

**RMA Support**

* Receive, inspect, and log inbound RMA replacement parts against open vendor cases.
* Package, label, and ship failed or defective components back to vendors within required return windows.
* Prepare RMA shipping documentation and coordinate carrier pickups for vendor returns.
* Update RMA records with tracking numbers, serial numbers, and shipment status.
* Maintain organized, clearly labeled storage for RMA spares, pending returns, and defective parts.
* Partner with the RMA Coordinator II to resolve shipping discrepancies and keep RMA cases moving.

**Ticketing & Vendor Coordination**

* Open and manage CoreSite tickets for Jenny orders and related facility requests.
* Coordinate with vendors, carriers, and data center personnel to support operational activities.
* Track ticket status and ensure timely completion of service requests.

**Asset & Inventory Management**

* Manage asset tracking for customer consignments and internal company equipment.
* Apply asset tags and maintain accurate asset documentation and inventory records.
* Track hardware lifecycle information including deployment, storage, return, and disposal status.
* Conduct inventory audits and assist with reconciliation activities.
* Maintain accurate records within asset management systems and spreadsheets.

Experience & Qualifications
---------------------------

**Required**

* High school diploma or equivalent required; technical certifications or related education preferred.
* 2+ years of experience in technical operations, warehouse coordination, IT support, or facilities operations preferred.
* Basic understanding of networking hardware, server equipment, and infrastructure environments.
* Experience with shipping/logistics processes and inventory management.
* Ability to lift and move equipment safely in warehouse and deployment environments.
* Familiarity with ticketing systems, inventory systems, and asset tracking tools.
* Valid driver’s license preferred for shipping drop-offs and local operational support.

**Preferred**

* Strong organizational and multitasking skills
* Hands-on technical troubleshooting ability
* Detail-oriented with strong documentation practices
* Ability to work independently and manage priorities effectively

* Customer service mindset with responsiveness and professionalism
